title: The close-out calls CI 'unsatisfiable by waiting' when it merely asked too early
description:
3q0 opened epic PR #11 and refused it the SAME SECOND:

    closeout_ci_absent: no CI has run on the epic PR #11: .github/workflows/ci.yml
    has produced no check runs on its head, so the close-out's precondition is
    unsatisfiable by waiting — the workflow may not trigger on pull_request at all

Every part of that diagnosis is wrong. ci.yml has a bare `pull_request:` trigger with no branch filter, and it ran on PRs #8, #9 and #10 earlier the same day. Forty-five seconds after the refusal, all four checks were present and running.

GitHub had simply not created the check runs yet. The close-out opened the PR and asked about it within a second.

The damage is the WORDING, not the wait. 'Unsatisfiable by waiting' is the one verdict that tells an operator not to bother waiting, and it volunteers a false cause — that the workflow may not trigger at all — which sends whoever reads it to edit a workflow file that is correct. An unattended run would stop here permanently, and the person who came to look would be handed a wrong lead.

This is the mirror of 9da. There the close-out asked about a head that kept moving; here it asks before an answer can exist. Both are the close-out treating a MOMENTARY absence of CI as a PERMANENT fact.

Work:
- A PR opened by this run has no CI yet BY CONSTRUCTION. Wait for check runs to appear before concluding anything, bounded, and say 'waiting for CI to appear' while doing so.
- Only after that bound expires may the run suggest the workflow might not trigger — and it should then say what it checked, not guess.
- Never let one absent-CI code carry both 'too early' and 'never coming'. They have opposite repairs.
- Test: open a PR, ask immediately, assert the run waits rather than refusing.

Found 2026-09-19 closing Phase 4.
